quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: Which light means you should slow down and be careful at an intersection?

options.text: A flashing yellow light
A flashing red light
A solid yellow light
A solid red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing yellow light
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be ready to stop. Look both ways before entering the intersection.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.
Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.
Allow the motorcycle to use only half of a lane.
Pass using the same lane as the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle needs a full lane to ride safely. Even if there seems to be room to share the lane, motorcyclists need space to move and balance safely.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the road edge. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.
Speed up and steer back onto the pavement gradually.
Slam on your brakes and stop.
Slow down gently with the brakes. Then turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gently with the brakes. Then turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement safely.
questions.explanation: Keep your wheels off the pavement and gently tap the brakes to slow down. Once you are at a safe speed, turn the wheel smoothly to get back on the road. Do not jerk the wheel suddenly.

questions.question: A bus is signaling to merge back into the road after stopping. You must:

options.text: Honk to let them know you're there.
Move to the left lane.
Yield.
Speed up to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield.
questions.explanation: You must yield to a bus that is merging back into traffic. Change lanes, slow down, or stop to let the bus safely rejoin the road.

questions.question: Your blind spot is:

options.text: An area you cannot see without turning your head.
Directly behind your vehicle.
The area you see in your rearview mirror.
The area you see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: An area you cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. They are beside and behind your vehicle. You must turn your head to see them.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Drive slowly and carefully.
Not use high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to see better.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Fog makes it hard to see. Slow down and be careful. Use low beam headlights—high beams reflect off the fog and make it worse. Drive at a reduced speed.

questions.question: Roads become very slippery:

options.text: When it has been raining for an hour or more.
The day after it rains.
During the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.
Right after the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery in the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain. Rain brings oil from the asphalt to the surface, making the road very slick. Heat makes this worse.

questions.question: A driver entering a highway from an on-ramp should:

options.text: Yield to drivers already on the highway.
Have the right-of-way.
Force their way into traffic.
Expect other drivers to move out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the highway.
questions.explanation: When you enter a highway on an acceleration ramp, you must yield to cars already on the highway. Merge safely when you have an opening.

questions.question: A yellow and black diamond-shaped sign:

options.text: Warns you about conditions on or near the road.
Directs you to cities and towns.
Tells you about traffic laws.
Tells you about construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warns you about conditions on or near the road.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs with black symbols on a yellow background are warning signs. They tell you about hazards or conditions ahead on the road.

questions.question: Keeping space around your vehicle is important because it:

options.text: Prevents distractions from other vehicles.
Gives you time to react to problems.
Keeps traffic moving at a safe speed.
Keeps other drivers alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react to problems.
questions.explanation: Extra space around your vehicle gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. This is the safest way to avoid crashes.

questions.question: What does this sign prevent?

options.text: Entering full parking lots.
Entering road construction areas.
Entering dead-end streets.
Entering one-way streets and expressway ramps from the wrong direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Entering one-way streets and expressway ramps from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that the road is one-way. You cannot enter from your current direction.

questions.question: To turn left from a multi-lane, one-way street or highway, start from which lane?

options.text: The middle of the intersection.
The right lane.
The left lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: Always start from the left lane when turning left on multi-lane streets and highways.

questions.question: Checking your blind spot by turning your head before changing lanes, leaving a curb, or merging into traffic is:

options.text: A bad driving habit.
A good driving habit.
Unnecessary.
Not necessary if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: A good driving habit.
questions.explanation: Always check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder before changing lanes. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: You are waiting in an intersection to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights to signal other drivers.
Drive around a car blocking you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If hit from behind, this prevents you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: An object is on the roadway.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road is curving sharply to the left.
A merge point is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is curving sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: Chevron signs show a sharp curve in the direction of the arrow. In this case, the road curves sharply to the left. You may see several of these signs through the curve.

questions.question: You reach an intersection where you want to turn, but you are not in the proper lane. What should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your signal and make the turn from your current lane.
Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
Safely change lanes and put your vehicle in reverse to go back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make last-minute turns. Drive to the next intersection and turn from the proper lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop ahead.
Buggy warning.
Limited parking.
Do not block intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells you that a stop sign is coming ahead. Prepare to stop completely before you go.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Keep the same speed.
Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: Slow down when a driver wants to pass you. This gives them enough room to complete the pass quickly and safely.

questions.question: What is true about drowsy drivers?

options.text: They should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
They may drive so poorly they appear drunk.
They can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
They are usually only older drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may drive so poorly they appear drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers may drive so poorly that they appear drunk. Opening a window, turning up the radio, or drinking coffee is not enough to keep a drowsy driver alert.

questions.question: When must you yield for emergency vehicles?

options.text: Under no circumstances.
When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
Only when other vehicles yield.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights.

questions.question: You hear a siren while driving but cannot see the emergency vehicle yet. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and look to see if the vehicle is on your street.
Slow down. Do not stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if the vehicle is on your street.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or horn but cannot see the emergency vehicle, safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop. Wait until you are sure the vehicle is not coming toward you.

questions.question: A driver taking a non-prescription drug should:

options.text: Read the labels on the drug before driving.
Drink alcohol instead.
Continue to drive regardless of any warning labels.
Drive only during daylight hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the labels on the drug before driving.
questions.explanation: Over-the-counter medications can affect your ability to drive safely. Check the label for warnings before driving. If you are unsure, ask your doctor or pharmacist if the medication is safe to use while driving.

questions.question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass another vehicle?

options.text: Yes.
No.
Yes, if there is no oncoming traffic.
Yes, if the vehicle ahead is driving under the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: No.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean neither direction can cross them. You can only cross them when turning into a driveway or business entrance. Passing over solid yellow lines is never allowed.

questions.question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
Drivers must use hand signals to communicate with each other.
One driver should proceed without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles normally proceed in the order they arrive. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: You are driving on a divided multilane highway and see or hear an emergency vehicle's signal. What should you do?

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as quickly as you can.
Slow down, move to create a clear path for the emergency vehicle, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to create a clear path for the emergency vehicle, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, slow down, clear a path, and stop. Do not try to outrun the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: Driving while distracted usually:

options.text: Is never dangerous.
Causes the driver to react more slowly to hazards.
Causes the driver to drive faster.
Is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Causes the driver to react more slowly to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions slow down your reaction time to traffic and road hazards. Distracted driving is never safe.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a hill or incline with a curb, how should you position your wheels?

options.text: Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.
Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.
Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
Keep your front wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill, turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb to prevent your vehicle from rolling into traffic. On streets without a curb, turn the wheels sharply toward the edge of the road.

questions.question: When checking your tires, what should you look for?

options.text: Tread that is not worn away.
Air pressure that is not too low.
No flat spots.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Check your tires before driving. Make sure the tread is not worn, the air pressure is correct, and the tires are not flat. Poor tire condition makes driving unsafe.

questions.question: What does a red circle with a slash through it on a regulatory sign mean?

options.text: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
An action is forbidden.
Some drivers must yield to others.
Drivers should drive under the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: An action is forbidden.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs with a red circle and slash forbid a specific action. These rectangular signs are white with red and black markings. The red circle and slash on a symbol means that action is not allowed.

questions.question: Why should you use extra caution when driving near a pedestrian with a white cane?

options.text: The person is deaf.
The person is a police officer.
The person is blind.
The person has poor balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: The person is blind.
questions.explanation: A white cane means the pedestrian is blind. Slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be ready to stop. Be prepared to avoid injury to the pedestrian.

questions.question: When should drivers use hand-to-hand steering?

options.text: When turning the wheel during normal driving.
When avoiding a hazard at high speed.
When turning the wheel at low speeds.
When backing, signaling, using the radio, or operating windshield wipers.

questions.correctAnswerText: When turning the wheel during normal driving.
questions.explanation: Use hand-to-hand steering while driving normally at speeds above 15 mph. This is also called push-pull steering.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Proceed slowly through the intersection.
Stop, then go when the road is clear.
Stop, then go when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
You can turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must come to a complete stop. Stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears, unless a sign says otherwise.

questions.question: What are hurricane evacuation route signs?

options.text: Signs on highways that should be used if there is a hurricane evacuation.
Signs that are only posted when a hurricane is happening.
Signs recommended only for visitors from out of state.
Signs recommended only for Louisiana residents.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signs on highways that should be used if there is a hurricane evacuation.
questions.explanation: Hurricane evacuation route signs show which highways to use in an emergency. Learn where these signs are in your area in case of an emergency.

questions.question: How should you prepare for hazards ahead?

options.text: Look at the entire road and both sides of the road.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Focus only on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the entire road and both sides of the road.
questions.explanation: You can handle dangerous situations better if you spot problems early. Look far ahead and scan the entire road, including both sides. Do not just stare at the center of the road.

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until the children wave to you before proceeding.
Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
Speed up quickly.
Turn on your emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus with its stop arm extended and lights flashing, watch for children on the sides of the road. Always drive carefully near children.

questions.question: What happens if a bicyclist breaks traffic laws?

options.text: Nothing happens because bicyclists do not have to follow traffic laws.
They can be ticketed.
They will always get a warning.
Their bicycle will be taken away.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can be ticketed.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights, duties, and responsibilities as car drivers. Both car drivers and bicyclists can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots?

options.text: By looking in your side mirrors.
By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
By looking in your rearview mirror.
By looking straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Check them by turning your head and looking over your shoulders.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for trucks.
Do not pass trucks.
Truck parking area ahead.
Steep downgrade ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downgrade ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill is ahead.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Turn on your hazard lights.
You can drive at the maximum speed limit.
Do not drive faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights when visibility drops to 500 feet or less. Use low beams in fog or rain. High beams reflect light back into your eyes and reduce visibility.

questions.question: When can a driver legally pass on the right?

options.text: If the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane available.
Even if it means driving off the pavement.
On a narrow bridge.
At any time.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane available.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right if there is a passing lane and the vehicle is turning left or waiting to turn left. You can also pass on the right on roads with two or more lanes in the same direction. Never drive off the pavement to pass another vehicle.
